_comment: Sample article. Its job is to make the first launch honest: a fresh install with no API key must still have something to read, hear, and tap. Structure mirrors the real writer's output (DESIGN §10) so swapping in a written article is a file swap, not a migration. Marked words are a tier, never a verdict — 'unfamiliar' gets the vermilion pencil rule, 'difficult' gets the jade one. There is no 'known'.
title: What a Pointer Really Is

sentences.en: Most beginners meet pointers in the second week of C, and most beginners hate them.
sentences.cn: 大多数初学者在学习 C 的第二周就会遇到指针，而且大多数初学者都讨厌它们。

sentences.en: That is fair, because the word arrives before the idea behind it.
sentences.cn: 这种感觉很合理，因为这个词比它背后的概念先到。

sentences.en: A pointer is just a variable that stores an address.
sentences.cn: 指针只是一个存放地址的变量。

sentences.en: An address is a number that says where a value lives in memory.
sentences.cn: 地址是一个数字，它说明某个值存放在内存的哪里。

sentences.en: When you write int x = 5, the compiler reserves a small block of memory and puts 5 inside it.
sentences.cn: 当你写下 int x = 5 时，编译器会预留一小块内存，并把 5 放进去。

sentences.en: To read the value, you dereference the pointer, and the star gives you 5 back.
sentences.cn: 要读取那个值，你对指针解引用，星号就把 5 还给你。

sentences.en: If you dereference a pointer that was never set, your program crashes with a segmentation fault.
sentences.cn: 如果你解引用一个从未设置过的指针，程序会崩溃，并抛出一个段错误。

sentences.en: You can also allocate memory yourself, because malloc asks the heap for a block.
sentences.cn: 你也可以自己分配内存，因为 malloc 是向堆申请一块空间。

sentences.en: Forget free and the memory leaks, a little on every loop, until the program runs out.
sentences.cn: 忘掉 free，内存就会泄漏，每次循环漏一点，直到程序用光为止。

sentences.en: None of this is clever. It is a book-keeping habit, and the compiler follows it exactly.
sentences.cn: 这些都不算聪明。它只是一个记账习惯，而编译器会严格照做。

sentences.en: Read the value through the pointer and you will never mix the two up again.
sentences.cn: 透过指针读取那个值，你就再也不会把这两者搞混了。
